et ciffer.explanation: "Et ciffer" means "a digit". Do not mix it up with "et tal" (a number). To say how many digits a number has, say: "Tallet 25 har to cifre" (The number 25 has two digits).

et cirkus.explanation: "Et cirkus" means "a circus". When you talk about a chaotic situation, it also means "a mess": "Det er et cirkus herhjemme" (It is a circus at home).

et citat.explanation: "Et citat" means "a quote". It comes from the verb "at citere" (to quote). To talk about a well-known one, say: "Det er et berømt citat fra Shakespeare" (It is a famous quote from Shakespeare).

et computerspil.explanation: "Et computerspil" means "a computer game". It is built from "en computer" (a computer) and "et spil" (a game). To say you play one, use "spille" (play): "Han spiller computerspil" (He plays computer games).

et cpr-nummer.explanation: "Et CPR-nummer" means "a CPR number". CPR stands for "Det Centrale Personregister" (the Central Person Register). In Denmark, it is the personal ID number that residents are given.

et crush.explanation: "Et crush" means "a crush". The word is borrowed from English. To say who the crush is on, use "på" (on): "Jeg har et crush på en kollega" (I have a crush on a coworker).

et cv.explanation: "Et cv" means "a CV". It is written in lowercase, and the endings come after an apostrophe: "cv'et" (the CV). To say you send one, use "sende" (send): "Jeg sender mit cv til firmaet" (I send my CV to the company).

et cykelbud.explanation: "Et cykelbud" means "a bike courier". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et bud" (a messenger).

et cykelløb.explanation: "Et cykelløb" means "a bike race". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et løb" (a race). The end "løb" is also in "et maratonløb" (a marathon).

et cykelstativ.explanation: "Et cykelstativ" means "a bike rack". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et stativ" (a stand).

at dampe.explanation: "At dampe" means "to steam". It comes from "damp" (steam). When you talk about cooking, it also means to cook in steam: "Jeg damper grøntsager" (I steam vegetables).

at danne.explanation: "At danne" means "to form". To say people start a government, say: "De danner en regering" (They form a government). Do not mix it up with "at forme" (to shape with your hands): "Jeg former dejen" (I shape the dough).

at danse.explanation: "At danse" means "to dance". To say who you dance with, use "med" (with): "Jeg danser med Anna" (I dance with Anna).

at date.explanation: "At date" means "to date", as in seeing someone romantically. Do not mix it up with "en dato" (a date on the calendar): "Hvad er datoen i dag?" (What is the date today?).

at debattere.explanation: "At debattere" means "to debate". To say what people debate, say: "Vi debatterer skolereformen" (We are debating the school reform). Do not mix it up with "at diskutere" (to discuss): "Vi diskuterer, hvad vi skal spise" (We are discussing what to eat).

at definere.explanation: "At definere" means "to define". To say you set a clear goal, use it with "et mål" (a goal): "Vi definerer et mål for året" (We define a goal for the year).

at dele.explanation: "At dele" means "to share / divide". When you share something with a person, add "med" (with): "Jeg deler min mad med dig" (I share my food with you). When you divide numbers, use "delt med" (divided by): "Ti delt med to er fem" (Ten divided by two is five).

at dele ud.explanation: "At dele ud" means "to hand out". It is built from "at dele" (to share) and "ud" (out). To say what is handed out, say: "Læreren deler opgaverne ud" (The teacher hands out the assignments). Do not mix it up with "at dele" (to share), where people use the same thing together: "Vi deler en pizza" (We share a pizza).

at delegere.explanation: "At delegere" means "to delegate". To name the person you pass the task to, add "til" (to): "Hun delegerer opgaven til Lars" (She delegates the task to Lars).

at deltage.explanation: "At deltage" means "to participate". To say what you take part in, add "i" (in): "Jeg deltager i mødet" (I am taking part in the meeting).

at demonstrere.explanation: "At demonstrere" means "to demonstrate". When you show how something works, say: "Læreren demonstrerer forsøget" (The teacher demonstrates the experiment). When you talk about a protest, it also means "to protest": "Folk demonstrerer foran Christiansborg" (People are demonstrating in front of Christiansborg, the parliament building).

at designe.explanation: "At designe" means "to design". The person who designs is "en designer" (a designer).

at dirigere.explanation: "At dirigere" means "to conduct / direct". When you lead an orchestra, say: "Han dirigerer orkestret" (He conducts the orchestra). When you point the way for cars, say: "Politiet dirigerer trafikken" (The police are directing traffic). For a film, use "at instruere" (to direct a film) instead: "Hun instruerer en film" (She directs a film).

at diskutere.explanation: "At diskutere" means "to discuss". To say people argue angrily, use "at skændes" (to quarrel): "De skændes hele tiden" (They quarrel all the time).

at distrahere.explanation: "At distrahere" means "to distract". To say someone does it on purpose, say: "Tyven distraherede vagten" (The thief distracted the guard).
